_what: Example of McpServer/OutlookAI.McpServer.Tests/live-fixtures/live-test-settings.json, which is gitignored and must stay that way - it names real stores and this repository is public. Copy this file there and replace every value. Keys are matched case-insensitively and unknown keys are ignored, so the _-prefixed notes below are safe to keep or delete. Every address in this file is under the RFC 2606 .invalid domain, and .github/scripts/check-testbed-references.ps1 check 8 fails the build if one ever is not.
_shape: This is the PORTABLE (test-guest) shape. Since 2026-09-24 it carries 'probeTerm' and a complete 'subjectOnlyProbe' block too: a test guest's hub holds a GENERATED population (corpus-build --population hub) that contains exactly such a population, and the values below are the generator's own - read them off 'corpus-plan --population hub', never invent them. A Production profile REQUIRES both, and may carry an optional 'delegateNestedFolderProbe' block { storeDisplayName, folderName, comParentPath }, which no test machine has.
_partialBlocksAreRejected: corpus, mailSink and subjectOnlyProbe are all-or-nothing. A block with three fields out of four reads as configured and behaves as absent, which is exactly the silence these checks exist to remove - so the loader throws instead.
_hubPopulation: The manifest of the population generated into the hub (corpus-build --population hub), named corpus-<id>.jsonl after the id Testbed/testbed.json's corpusIdConvention.populations assigns this guest's hub. On a test guest the hub is REBUILT BEFORE EVERY RUN from it - Testbed/guest/Reset-HubPopulation.ps1 - because the index frontier test can catch a local-time misreading only while the hub's newest item is younger than the machine's UTC offset; that test reads this manifest and fails with the remedy on a hub nobody rebuilt. Leave the key out on a machine whose hub holds no generated population - the maintainer's own, whose hub is real mail - and the test says what it could not prove instead.
_watched: expectedStoreDisplayNames is the WATCHED list: every store the tier profile mounts. It is what the count tripwire censuses (with the bystander and delegate lists unioned in), what the identity-draft grant is drawn from, what list_accounts exactness counts and what outlook_health must reach. It does NOT say a store is indexed - that is the next list.
_indexed: indexedStoreDisplayNames is the INDEXED list: the stores the index-tier tests measure, each of which must be discoverable in the search index with mail in it. Every entry must also be watched; never a delegate mailbox. Order is read: the HUB FIRST (several index tests read entry 0, and the hub population is the one carrying senders and attachments), the corpus store LAST (the exclude-subfolders measurement reads the first non-hub entry, and only the bystander population has subfolders). Name every indexed store except the dominant corpus AS AN ADDRESS: the product finds a small store in the index only by mail addressed to it, and only for a name shaped like an address. Absent means 'the same as the watched list', which is what every settings file written before 2026-09-24 meant. On a guest whose index is switched off it is [].
_bystanders: The stores the count tripwire exists to watch: watched, and written to by NOTHING. Naming a store here denies it every kind of write, keeps it in the census, and takes it out of the identity tests' account list. The tier watches a declared bystander even if expectedStoreDisplayNames leaves it out - the census adds declared bystanders back in - but name it there too, as here: that list is also what outlook_health's reachability check and list_accounts exactness read, and a store missing from it is one they never look for. Naming the hub here is refused at the top of the run, not resolved. On a Production profile the delegate mailboxes are already denied and already watched, so they need no declaration.
_bystandersAreMANDATORY: The live tier REFUSES to start when this leaves the census nothing it could fail on - no watched store that is both non-hub and denied every write. There is no flag that turns that refusal off. It is not a formality: the run it used to allow censused every folder, identified nothing and printed '0 failure(s)' whatever had happened to the mail. If the refusal fires it names the two keys to edit.
_corpusStoresAreBystandersToo: The measurement corpus store is declared here as well, and it matters more than it looks. No live test writes to a corpus: LiveCorpusFreshness only reads the manifest, and rebuilding a stale corpus is an operator action from the accountless profile. Left undeclared, a corpus store listed in expectedStoreDisplayNames is inside the identity-draft grant purely for being a non-hub primary - so the identity tests would create drafts in the measurement corpus the moment this machine gains a mail account. Declaring it makes that a refusal instead. Declare only corpus stores THIS Outlook profile actually mounts: a declared store the profile does not have is watched, cannot be censused, and refuses the tier. Corpus B lives on the other guest (Docs/live-tier-on-the-vm.md section 1.1a), so it belongs in THAT guest's settings file, declared the same way - not here.
_theSweepNoLongerDependsOnThisDeclaratio: Until 2026-08-25 the post-run artifact sweep was the second reason to declare a corpus store: it matches on the [OutlookAI-McpTest] tag, which every corpus subject also carried, so it would have found the whole corpus and tried to DELETE it - and declaring the store only downgraded that to a write-guard refusal, i.e. a permanently red sweep on this machine. Corpus items now carry their own tag, [OutlookAI-Corpus], and no corpus subject contains the text OutlookAI-McpTest anywhere, so the sweep cannot match one whatever this file says. That holds for the generated hub and bystander populations too, which carry the corpus tag. Keep the declaration for the identity-draft half above. A corpus built BEFORE that date still carries the old tag; the corpus tooling recognises it, refuses, and says to rebuild.
_probeTerm: A word the index is proven to hit in every indexed store, and in one text attachment of the hub. On a test guest it is the generator's CorpusPopulation.ProbeTerm - in the body vocabulary of every population and of the measurement corpus. Empty on a guest with no index.

subjectOnlyProbe._note: The SF-6 recall regression's population: every item in folderPath carries subjectTerm in its SUBJECT and in no body, and comes from the one sender whose name and address carry senderFragment. On a test guest it is the hub population's Notices folder; storeDisplayName is the hub. Leave the block out on a guest with no index.

corpus._note: The four identity values must match Testbed/testbed.json. manifestPath is machine-local and is the ONLY thing that can tear the corpus down - keep a copy outside the guest.

mailSink._note: Loopback submission and retrieval. Absent means this machine has real transport. Ports are whatever the sink was configured with; nothing needs the well-known numbers. See Testbed/README.md question 11 before assuming the retrieval side is POP3.
